reasoning: Both are well-structured, typed, and tear down properly. B has a real correctness bug: _Hide clears _IsPlaceable without restyling, so after hiding over a valid spot the ghost can reappear over a blocked spot without the red tint. A reapplies the style every frame, so it never shows the wrong colour, and its destroy is guarded. B's query shape is slightly nicer, but A works correctly.

criteria.note: _update raycasts every render step, filters { character, self._part }, snaps result.Position + Normal*BlockSize/2, unparents on miss, checks against PlacedBlocks, and _applyStyle is reapplied each frame and on setBlockType, so the tint is always current.
destroy unbinds the render step, destroys the part, and is guarded by _destroyed, so a frame can't run on a destroyed ghost; there are no other connections.
A Fields type is cast in setmetatable({...} :: Fields), all fields are set in the constructor, methods are called with a colon, and the part has CanCollide/CanQuery false and is also in the filter.
Everything is typed with BlockTypes.BlockType; getPlacement returns (Vector3?, boolean) with the centre non-nil even when blocked, which is consistent and documented but a bit less tidy.
A named Options {transparency, maxDistance} table with DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY/DEFAULT_MAX_DISTANCE constants and validation.
A single class file, shared modules untouched, and all tools pass; the 'disconnect' check miss is a false negative because the render step is unbound.

Raycast, half-block offset, snap, and check are correct, but _Hide sets _IsPlaceable=false without _ApplyStyle, so after hiding over a valid spot the ghost reappears over a blocked spot in its normal colour instead of red.
Destroy unbinds the render step, disconnects _CharacterAddedConnection, and destroys the part; there is no destroyed guard, but a repeat call is harmless.
The typeof(setmetatable({} :: {...})) type lists all fields set in the constructor, and the part has CanQuery=false; the hidden part stays parented in workspace at transparency 1.
Typed constructor and methods using BlockType; GetPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?) with nil whenever it isn't placeable.
A named Options {Transparency, RayLength} table with DEFAULT_ constants and asserts.
A single class, shared modules unchanged, and all tools pass.

strengths: Correct per-frame tint and visibility logic
Idempotent destroy with a destroyed guard
Filter rebuilt each frame handles respawns without extra connections
weaknesses: getPlacement returns a position even when it isn't placeable, so callers must check the boolean

strengths: CharacterAdded keeps the filter current and is disconnected on Destroy
Only updates CFrame and style on change
weaknesses: Stale tint bug: after a hide, a blocked spot can show in the normal colour
The ghost itself isn't in the raycast filter (relies on CanQuery only)
